title: Enable `st.dataframe` to handle dataframes with hierarchical headers
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When displaying a transposed dataframe using `st.dataframe` the upper indices get a ⚠️ on the labels. This was not the case with previous streamlit releases. 

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://<redacted-host>/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://<redacted-host>/?issue=gh-6319)

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st


labels = [
    ["Aiyana", "Aiyana", "Anisha", "Anisha"],
    ["Mathematics", "Science", "Mathematics", "Science"]
]
tuples = list(zip(*labels))
index = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(tuples, names=["Students", "Subjects"])
df = pd.DataFrame([
    [98, 95, 99],
    [95, 93, 96],
    [92, 99, 95],
    [99, 95, 97]
], index=index, columns=["1st term", "2nd term", "Final"])

# works as expected for a dataframe
st.dataframe(df)


# transposing..... shows weird results
st.dataframe(df.T)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Show transposed dataframe without additional unicode in the table. 

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version (streamlit 1.15).

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.20.0
- Python version: 3.10.10
- Operating System: Fedora Linux 37
- Browser: Brave


### Additional Information

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/97027589/225307290-3b909541-d620-4f97-b531-4a24399a8261.png)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @reporter Thanks for reporting this issue. I was able to reproduce this. Previous versions were indeed able to handle multi-header dataframes slightly better (showing it without the warning), but it wasn't really an officially supported feature. We might need to investigate adding official support for multiple header columns in the future.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Meanwhile, my workaround is to use `streamlit.markdown` with `pandas.Styler` as I do [around here in Investorzilla](https://github.com/participant2/investorzilla/blob/9184cb4a8df86e2fc7f608df90e74e5a41096af3/investorzilla/streamlit_ui.py#L321):

```python
df=pandas.DataFrame(...)

# CSS to highlight headers and index of the dataframe
table_styles=[
    dict(selector="th",       props="font-size: 0.8em; "),
    dict(selector="td",       props="font-size: 0.8em; text-align: right"),
    dict(selector='tr:hover', props='background-color: yellow')
]

streamlit.markdown(
    df

    # Make pandas.Styler from the DataFrame
    .style

    # Negative numbers in red
    .apply(
        lambda cell: numpy.where(cell<0, "color: red", None),
        axis=1
    )

    # Apply CSS
    .set_table_styles(table_styles)

    # Convert DataFrame Styler object to formatted HTML text
    .to_html(),

    # Streamlit stop complaining
    unsafe_allow_html=True
)
```

Result is a semi-interactive table like the following

![Investorzilla hierarchical table](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/3484242/a1756324-a677-4ce7-8429-11e3cdf8f478)

Screenshot taken from one of [Investorzilla](https://github.com/participant2/investorzilla)'s reports.

Not ideal, but pretty good.
